A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Language-Mixed CoT, YI-SANG and KO-REAson study. The main text, tables, figures and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison. A localized caption overlap in v2 does not prevent recovering the content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, training-data and CoT ablations, and English and multimodal transfer results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds translated-data, anchor-language, teacher-choice and larger-training-mixture experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed English/Korean CoT supervision, Qwen3-32B distillation and final YI-SANG-HQ training recipe remain unchanged. Alternative teachers and languages are additional experimental variants. Expanded decontamination documentation does not establish a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Chinese/Korean and Russian/Korean reasoning supervision and an experiment incorporating untranslated English OpenThought prompts. The main Korean benchmark suite and Appendix D transfer evaluations remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds DeepSeek-R1-32B-supervised students to the teacher comparison, although DeepSeek already appeared in the main model comparison. Table 2 also adds Russian- and Chinese-anchored variants alongside the retained monolingual and English/Korean alternatives.

E3.justification: New settings include five-epoch Qwen2.5-1.5B training on translated OpenThoughts-114K and Gemma3-4B training with 500k additional English examples. Existing splits, metrics and decoding settings are retained. The larger mixture's stated 780k total is inconsistent with the reported 260k plus 500k components.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the recipe's design choices: translated-data effects on cultural competence, Chinese/Russian versus English anchoring, distillation from another teacher family, and a larger English-data mixture (Tables 1, 2, 7 and 10). These complement the retained category, augmentation, packing and subset-scaling analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify single evaluations for ablations and three independent trials with mean and standard error for main results. No new seed disclosures, uncertainty procedures or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Four added or expanded comparisons substantially extend the reported findings while retaining existing main scores. Table 1 reports translated-data training changing MATH from 25.48 to 74.35 and HRB from 35.24 to 15.34. Table 10 reports MCLM-Ko increasing from 55.0 to 67.4 while KMMLU-Redux and HRB decline. Tables 2 and 7 add anchor-language and teacher results. These are newly reported experimental comparisons, not v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The added terminology clarification and decontamination explanation introduce no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims about Language-Mixed CoT, the Korean dataset, competitive 4B-35B models, and cross-lingual and multimodal transfer. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a pretraining-mixture hypothesis for anchor-language effects, interprets student performance as teacher-dependent, and explains rejecting the larger English mixture because of its math-versus-Korean-performance tradeoff. It also explains avoiding embedding-based decontamination because of computational cost and possible removal of legitimate background knowledge.

D1.justification: Where v1 only states 13-gram decontamination, v2 documents MeCab-KO segmentation and normalization, checking prompts and reasoning traces, and separate raw-text and normalized-text passes with removal upon any match. These are newly disclosed implementation details; existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts and release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds representation-alignment approaches citing Zhu et al., Lai and Nissim, and Chen et al. New citations also support anchor-language selection and MeCab-KO processing. The central positioning around native Korean prompts and mixed-language supervision is retained.

P1.justification: Section 2 becomes 'Preliminaries and Related Works,' several explanatory passages and Appendix A.4 expand, and a duplicated filtering paragraph is removed. Affiliations are updated and acknowledgments removed. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 1, 7 and 10 and expands the CoT table with two anchor-language rows. Existing figures and tables are retained with relocation and reflow, including Figure 2 moving into related work. Figure 5's caption newly overlaps body text on v2 page 10.

improvement.justification: The added anchor-language, teacher and data-mixture experiments better support practical design choices, while the decontamination details improve reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement without changing the main results. The inconsistent larger-mixture sample count and new Figure 5 caption overlap are drawbacks.
